bull.t: Low leverage and stronger equity base
bull.b: Relatively low leverage and a sharply higher equity base provide greater solvency and financial flexibility than a highly debt-funded structure. This can help Cabaletta sustain development activity and absorb operating volatility while its clinical programs remain pre-commercial.

The large warrant exercise proceeds materially strengthen near-term liquidity and extend the resources available for research, clinical development, and operations. Greater cash flexibility may reduce immediate financing pressure while Cabaletta advances its autoimmune therapy pipeline.

A focused pipeline of engineered CAR T candidates addresses multiple serious autoimmune indications with substantial unmet medical needs. If clinical development succeeds, this specialization could create several opportunities from a common therapeutic approach rather than relying on one indication.

bear.t: No commercial revenue or approved products
bear.b: The absence of approved products and recurring sales means Cabaletta currently has no established commercial revenue engine. Its ability to create durable value therefore depends on successful clinical development, regulatory progress, and eventual product launches that remain uncertain.

Losses have expanded substantially over time as the company funds its clinical-stage operations without product revenue. Persistent and increasing losses raise the amount of capital required to reach commercialization and make future profitability dependent on disciplined spending and successful development outcomes.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn and financing dependence
bear.b: Operating and free cash outflows have worsened materially, with losses translating into substantial real cash consumption. Continued burn can shorten the funding runway and leave the company reliant on additional equity, warrants, or collaborations to maintain development programs.
